traits.notes: The seedling displays distinct alternate leaf arrangement and lanceolate leaves. Some leaves show minor damage in the form of holes and brownish spots. A pink identification tag is attached to the stem.

data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached singly at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides, clearly visible in images 2, 4, and 5)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are spaced apart along the elongated stem rather than bunched together)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf consists of a single blade attached to the stem via a petiole)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (leaf margins appear smooth and continuous without teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaves are linear to lance-shaped, widest below the middle, and tapering to a point at both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (the leaf tip tapers to a slender point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (the leaf base tapers gradually to a wedge shape where it attaches to the petiole)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a central midrib is visible with secondary veins branching off laterally)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible (secondary veins branch off the midrib at an angle and are discernible on the leaf surface)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): glabrous (the leaf surface appears smooth and hairless)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no hairs or trichomes are visible on the leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (the petioles appear relatively short compared to the leaf blade length)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (the petioles appear cylindrical and round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (the stems appear thin, rigid, and brownish, characteristic of a woody seedling)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (the stems appear smooth and lack visible hairs)
    19. Stem color: brown (the stems are a light to medium brown color)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (the stems appear relatively smooth without prominent ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): unclear (stipules are not clearly visible at the leaf base in the provided images)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex is visible)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus is visible at the leaf base)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils are visible on the seedling)
F. Notes: The seedling displays distinct alternate leaf arrangement and lanceolate leaves. Some leaves show minor damage in the form of holes and brownish spots. A pink identification tag is attached to the stem.
